old_name: # analysis/naming2/ram2_renames.tsv -- RAM naming pass ram2: WRAM0 ($C000-$CFFF) and HRAM ($FF80-$FFFE) variables that were still neutral (wRam_CXXX / hRam_FFXX); kind is always const; HYPOTHESIS rows keep new_name == old_name and are not applied; evidence and reasoning in docs/research/naming2_ram2.md

evidence: minute threshold of the next warning on timer A: set to $09 with C26F:=0 at session starts (68:7060 Registration_Verify_RunState, Browser_LoadPage_* in page_loader.asm, 4E:5162 Browser_Menu_LinkLost, the 26/27 mail sessions); the time-warning test replicated 29 times in 13 files (68:71C3 Registration_Verify_StateAfterPopLogin, 26:4EC3 MailSession_CheckTimeWarning, page list/view/inline-image/mail-server loops) runs only while wTimerEnable bit4 (timer A clock), compares it with wTimerAMinutes (`cp` then wTimerASeconds >= $1E, so the threshold is reached at x:30) and on a hit adds $0A up to a cap of $45 and returns A=$FF (caller -> Registration_Verify_OnTimeLimit / CommNotice dialog); 2 independent earlier namers (g2 wConnWarnMinute, g7 wOnlineWarnMinute) read the same role; neutral 'TimerA' form chosen because what timer A measures is only PROBABLE

flag byte of the timer-A warning, always tested through `ld hl,$C26F` (114 raw uses in 13 banks): bit0 = warning raised/pending (set by the test at 68:71FC/26:4973 when a threshold is hit, tested first so a raised warning is not re-raised, cleared by CommNotice_ShowDialogMode0/1 7F:6218/6235 `res 0,[hl]` after the dialog), bit1 = final $45-minute warning already shown (set when wTimerAWarnMinute==$45, 68:71EC-71F7); Int_VBlank 00:03BA (`ld hl,$C26F ; res 1,[hl]`) clears bit1 when timer A reaches 70 minutes; cleared with C26E at session starts; same pair as wTimerAWarnMinute (g2 wConnWarnFlags / g7 wOnlineWarnFlags)
